title: Loss and Life Changes
summary: Grief, change of role, adjusting to change, and sources of support. Written in plain language for older adults.
clinicianNotes: Grief is normal. Use the summary only to guide a gentle conversation. Written for adults aged 60 and over. Topic areas are informed by general published work on stress, mood and wellbeing. All items are original wording and are not copied or adapted from any instrument. Bands are provisional and not clinically validated. Use the summary to guide your own questions. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist, and a topic-specific reference list should be added during that review.
prompt: Thinking about the last two weeks, how true is this for you?

guidance.ok: On grief, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On grief, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Allow the person to tell their story. Ask how long ago and how they are coping.
guidance.explore: On grief, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Allow the person to tell their story. Ask how long ago and how they are coping.

domains.label: Change of role
domains.description: Missing a former role or feeling less respected.

guidance.ok: On change of role, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On change of role, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore what the role meant and what could replace it.
guidance.explore: On change of role, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore what the role meant and what could replace it.

domains.label: Adjusting to change
domains.description: Difficulty with changes in living, health and independence.

guidance.ok: On adjusting to change, things look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: On adjusting to change, some strain is showing. Explore when it began, what triggers it, and what the person already does about it. Explore which change is hardest and what choice the person still has.
guidance.explore: On adjusting to change, the person is strongly affected. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted. Explore which change is hardest and what choice the person still has.

domains.label: Support and comfort
domains.description: People, faith and activities that help.

guidance.ok: On support and comfort, there is a strength to build on. Use it when planning next steps.
guidance.watch: On support and comfort, support is partly in place. Explore what helps and what gets in the way. Build on faith, people and activities that bring comfort.
guidance.explore: On support and comfort, support looks thin. Explore what is missing, who or what could help, and small first steps. Build on faith, people and activities that bring comfort.

items.text: I think a lot about someone I have lost.
It is hard to accept that this person is gone.
Reminders of my loss bring a wave of sadness.
I miss the role I used to have, such as work or running the household.
I feel less respected than I used to.
I feel my role in the family has changed in ways I do not like.
I find it hard to adjust to my living arrangements.
Changes in my health or independence worry me.
I feel I have lost control over my own life.
I have people I can talk to about my loss.
My faith or beliefs comfort me.
I am able to keep doing some activities that matter to me.
